title: Six-class rho on secp256k1 with 147-instruction ordinary-step budget

claims.statement: For uniform full-production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho attack specified in proof.md halts on every run after at most 2^127.00 target-group-operation equivalents: a global meter charges every action before it runs. The ordinary step is charged 1.147 units (the C=1000 reference addition plus the full 147-instruction row allowance, ten above the 137-instruction explicit sequence ledger); traversal costs 1.177 and doubling at most 2.0. Under the disclosed H1 random-mapping heuristic, the chance of recovery is greater than 0.3903 after a Markov early-halt bound below 0.0046 and all other loss events. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units and included; no nonuniform advice. The walk is unchanged from submission 758d8df6-df45-4684-9e49-5aa5e19e9089, itself derived from 189ebc42-1ef3-4232-8056-a34aad574d83 and 1c600df4; all are credited dependencies but no prior verdict is a mathematical premise. The experiment changes only a toy-order test that previously reduced r modulo r. This is an analytical, heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
